art.subject: Long-tailed Tit (Aegithalos caudatus caudatus), adult of the white-headed northern subspecies, as seen in Korea in winter: entire head, face, chin and throat pure white with no dark stripes; a black stripe down the centre of the back; scapulars dusky pink; wings blackish with broad white edges to the tertials and secondaries forming a white panel; underparts white, with a pinkish wash confined to the flanks; very long black tail with white outer feathers; tiny stubby black bill; dark eye; blackish legs.
art.pose: hanging from a thin willow twig in a small flock, side view, long tail hanging down
art.scene: Korean riverside woodland in winter with bare willows and birches under a pale sky; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a thin twig: round fluffy body, pure white head with no dark stripes, short stubby blackish bill, clear-cut black hindneck and upper mantle, pink scapulars, blackish wings with broad white tertial fringes, white underparts with a rosy flush only on the flanks, very long black tail with white outer feathers, blackish legs

adult, perched, rear three-quarter view with head and body facing the same way: all-white head, sharply defined black hindneck and upper mantle, pink scapulars, broad white tertial fringes on the blackish wing, very long graduated black tail edged white
art.build: Tiny round-bodied songbird with a very long tail; the body is smaller than a sparrow's, a fluffy ball with almost no visible neck, and the tail is longer than the head and body together. Bill tiny, stubby and conical, far shorter than the head. Legs short and blackish. Wings short and rounded, the wingtips reaching only the base of the tail. Tail long, narrow and graduated, black with white outer feathers. Moves in restless flocks, often hanging upside down from thin twigs.
avoid: Do not paint broad black stripes over the eyes - that is the resident Korean Long-tailed Tit; this subspecies has an all-white head.
Do not shorten the tail; it is longer than the body.
Do not paint a thick bill, a crest or yellow underparts.
Do not wash the breast and belly pink; in this white-headed subspecies the underparts are white, with pink only on the flanks.
